title: Architecture, data and behavior
subtitle: A fictional backend, from checkout to persistence

entities.name: Shopper
entities.summary: Places an order and follows its progress.
entities.description: A person using the sample storefront. The API accepts only the authenticated shopper identity, never an arbitrary customer ID from a request body.

entities.name: Support operator
entities.summary: Investigates order status with a read-only console.
entities.description: Uses the same API boundary with a support role. Refund and cancellation workflows are deliberately outside this introductory example.

entities.name: Storefront
entities.summary: Collects a basket and presents order status.
entities.description: Sends a unique request key when the shopper confirms a basket. A retry reuses that key so an uncertain network outcome does not create a second order.

entities.name: API gateway
entities.summary: Authenticates requests and forwards order commands.
entities.description: Checks the bearer token, applies rate limits, attaches a correlation ID, and routes to the Order API. Domain rules remain in the service.

entities.name: Order API
entities.summary: Owns order acceptance and the transactional outbox.
entities.description: Coordinates pricing, stock reservation and payment authorization. It commits the order and the pending OrderAccepted event in one database transaction. A declined authorization returns a failure and releases the reservation; that alternative is described in prose, not encoded as a second path in the sequence.

entities.name: Inventory service
entities.summary: Reserves sellable stock for a short window.
entities.description: A reservation is temporary until fulfillment confirms it. In this fictional design, reservation IDs make retries idempotent and expiry compensates for abandoned checkouts.

entities.name: Fulfillment worker
entities.summary: Consumes accepted orders and schedules packing.
entities.description: Consumes messages at least once, records handled event IDs, and sends a confirmation email. Acknowledges the message only after its durable work succeeds.

entities.name: Orders database
entities.summary: Stores orders, request keys and pending events.
entities.description: The Order API owns writes. The outbox relay is a loop inside the same service process in this small example; a production deployment could split it into a separate worker.

entities.name: Order event queue
entities.summary: Buffers accepted-order notifications.
entities.description: Delivery is at least once. Event IDs support deduplication; the queue does not promise exactly-once effects across the database, fulfillment system and email provider.

entities.name: Payment provider
entities.summary: Authorizes the final amount with an idempotency key.
entities.description: A successful authorization reserves funds; it is not a completed capture. Timeouts need reconciliation before the API decides whether to retry, fail or compensate.

entities.name: Email provider
entities.summary: Delivers the shopper confirmation.
entities.description: A delivery failure is retried by the background workflow. It must not reverse an already accepted order.

entities.name: Order
entities.summary: Aggregate root that protects accepted order invariants.
entities.description: A fictional teaching model. Status transitions are methods so callers cannot silently skip validation.

fields.name: id
fields.purpose: Stable identity across API, events and support.
fields.details: Generated once; opaque outside the order boundary.

fields.name: lines
fields.purpose: Snapshot of purchased items and agreed prices.
fields.details: A later catalog change does not rewrite the accepted order.

fields.name: status
fields.details: Changes through accept() and markPacking(), not direct assignment.

methods.name: accept()
methods.purpose: Checks totals and moves the order into Accepted.

methods.name: markPacking()
methods.purpose: Moves an accepted order into packing.

entities.name: OrderLine
entities.summary: Immutable purchase snapshot for one product.

fields.name: sku
fields.purpose: Connects a line to the reserved product.

fields.name: quantity
fields.purpose: Number of units promised to the shopper.

methods.name: subtotal()
methods.purpose: Computes quantity times the agreed price.

entities.name: Money
entities.summary: Value object for amounts and currency.

fields.name: minorUnits
fields.purpose: Stores cents or another currency minor unit.

fields.name: currency
fields.purpose: Identifies the currency used for arithmetic.

methods.name: add(other)
methods.purpose: Adds amounts after checking their currencies.

methods.name: multiply(quantity)
methods.purpose: Scales the amount by a whole item count.

entities.name: PlaceOrderService
entities.summary: Application coordinator for a checkout request.

fields.name: orders
fields.purpose: Loads existing request keys and commits orders.

methods.name: place(command)
methods.details: Idempotent lookup happens before a fresh attempt starts.

entities.name: OrderRepository
entities.summary: Persistence boundary used by the application service.

methods.name: findByRequestKey(key)
methods.purpose: Returns a prior result for a retried request.

methods.name: saveWithEvent(order, event)
methods.purpose: Atomically persists an order and its pending event.
methods.details: The adapter uses one database transaction.

entities.name: Regular input
entities.summary: No validation error is shown.
entities.description: The field can contain missing or invalid input until Save or field blur triggers validation. Regular describes the visible state, not a guarantee that the current value is valid.

entities.name: Input valid?
entities.summary: Check the current value when validation is triggered.
entities.description: Evaluate the value and retain which event triggered this check. A valid value returns to Regular input. Missing or invalid input enters the error state associated with Save or field blur.

entities.name: Error after Save
entities.summary: Save found missing or invalid input.
entities.description: Keep the error visible while the user types, even when the value becomes valid. Save does not clear this error. Only field blur with a valid value returns to Regular input; blur with an invalid value leaves the error unchanged.

entities.name: Error after blur
entities.summary: Field blur found missing or invalid input.
entities.description: Keep the error visible while the user types, even when the value becomes valid. Save does not clear this error. Only field blur with a valid value returns to Regular input; blur with an invalid value leaves the error unchanged.

entities.name: sales.order_headers
entities.summary: One accepted order per row.
entities.description: Fictional ORM record OrderRow. The database and code names differ deliberately; the row-level mapping columns make that relationship visible. This persistence model is separate from the domain types in the class view.

entities.name: sales.order_items
entities.summary: Purchased items and agreed prices.
entities.description: Fictional ORM record OrderItemRow. The composite key is (order_id, product_id). The product foreign key crosses into the Catalog module; stored price snapshots do not change when catalog pricing changes.

entities.name: catalog.products
entities.summary: Sellable products maintained by Catalog.
entities.description: Fictional ORM record ProductRow. Catalog owns writes; Ordering stores references and purchase snapshots. Physical identifiers and application properties are displayed independently rather than inferred from naming conventions.

diagrams.description: The successful checkout path. Fulfillment continues asynchronously after the response.

messages.label: Confirm basket
messages.description: The client keeps the same request key across retries.

messages.label: POST /orders + request key
messages.description: Payload contains SKU and quantity; the service determines trusted prices.

messages.label: Forward authenticated command
messages.description: Token checks and the correlation ID are applied at the edge.

messages.label: Find prior result by request key
messages.description: This happy path has no previous result. A replay returns the existing order.

messages.label: No existing order
messages.description: A unique database constraint also protects concurrent attempts.

messages.label: Reserve requested units
messages.description: Reserve against a short expiry with an idempotent reservation key.

messages.label: Reservation confirmed
messages.description: The example assumes all requested items are available.

messages.label: Authorize amount + request key
messages.description: Authorization reserves funds; later capture is outside this walkthrough.

messages.label: Authorization approved
messages.description: A timeout requires reconciliation because the external effect may have happened.

messages.label: Commit order + outbox event
messages.description: One transaction makes the order and pending event durable together.

messages.label: Transaction committed
messages.description: The accepted response can now refer to a durable order.

messages.label: 201 Created + order ID
messages.description: The gateway forwards the response to the storefront; two trivial forwarding arrows are omitted for space.

messages.label: Relay OrderAccepted from outbox
messages.description: The service relay may publish more than once after a crash. Consumers deduplicate by event ID.

messages.label: Deliver OrderAccepted
messages.description: Fulfillment records the event ID, schedules packing and sends the email shown in the overview.

diagrams.description: 40 entities in eight boundaries. The initial Overview fits the complete map; Read shows local detail. Search, zoom and selection reveal responsibilities without changing the shared model.

blocks.markdown: Explore a **fictional Order platform** through its responsibilities, runtime behavior, domain types, validation rules and stored data. These examples are illustrative, not findings from a production repository.

The Order API reserves stock, authorizes payment and commits an order with an outbox event. Fulfillment continues asynchronously. Groups distinguish people, owned services, durable data and external providers.

This explicit 14-message happy path adds the execution order that a static dependency map cannot supply. Phase captions organize the story. The accepted response follows the database commit; background delivery may happen later.

Application coordination, domain rules and persistence boundaries have different responsibilities. Purpose and Invariant columns explain each member. Composition and multiplicity describe ownership; the reusable Money value object keeps amount arithmetic explicit.

Save or field blur validates the current value. Once an error is visible, it clears **only when the value is correct and the field loses focus**. Typing alone or pressing Save keeps the error visible; invalid blur also leaves it unchanged.

Ordering owns order headers and item snapshots; Catalog owns products. Each item references **1** order and **1** product. An accepted order contains **1..n** items (an application rule); a product can appear in **0..n** items. Here **n** means many. The arrows follow **PK → FK**, while row columns map physical SQL names to code classes and properties.

This deliberately larger fictional landscape contains **40 entities and 44 selected relations**. It demonstrates grouped navigation rather than a recommended service decomposition. Use Overview for orientation, then Read, search or zoom for a useful local view.
